market_context.summary: Two shocks land in the same week and the regime has flipped. First, the Fed: August CPI (2026-09-11) printed 3.4% y/y headline and +0.3% m/m core, and the market now prices a 25bp HIKE at Wednesday's FOMC — CME FedWatch 85.6%, Kalshi 81% — against a 3.63% effective funds rate. The US 10-year traded 4.975% Friday and ~5.00% overnight, the highest since October 2023; the 2-year at ~4.65% is a two-year high and roughly 100bp ABOVE the funds rate, so the front end has stopped pricing cuts and started pricing hikes. It is not a US-only move: the German 10-year at 3.53% is the highest since 2009. Second, oil: the Strait of Hormuz has been closed since the war began 2026-02-28, and drones launched from Iraq hit the Saudi East-West pipeline on 2026-09-10/11, so the ~4-5m bbl/day reroute that had been working around Hormuz is now shut too. Both Saudi export routes are down simultaneously. Brent went toward $108 and WTI printed 102.52. Friday itself was an UP day — the S&P closed 7,656 (+0.86%), snapping a four-day losing streak as crude backed off — and the index sits less than 2% below its 120-day high. Overnight, S&P futures -0.5 to -0.7%, Nasdaq futures -1.2 to -1.7%, Nikkei -1.51%, Kospi -2.8%. The Nasdaq's double-sized decline is a second, independent shock: SoftBank fell 11-13% in Tokyo after Sam Altman ruled out an OpenAI IPO this year, with SK Hynix and Samsung both off more than 3.5%. Gold is the tell — it FELL to ~4,330 from 4,408.90 into a live war headline, because real yields are setting its price, not fear. The tape has already made the obvious macro moves: homebuilders are 16-19% off their highs, airlines 17-26%, defense 11-46%, and four of six AI names 22-42%, while the tankers are pinned at their 120-day highs. This is a tape that has repriced, not one that is repricing.

data_quality_notes:
RESEARCH RAN TO COMPLETION. notes.md carries a RESEARCH COMPLETE block at 06:27 ET superseding one at 06:22, so `truncated` is false and nothing here is reconstructed from fragments. Twelve candidate lines resolve to eleven distinct ideas — CCJ appears twice and the later line, carrying the corrected 86.00 stop, supersedes the first.

SHAPE OF THE DAY, AND IT IS UNUSUAL. All eleven ideas are `swing`. Zero intraday, zero long_term, and neither is a quota failure. Both long-term candidates were researched to a conclusion and rejected on their own arithmetic: MET (MetLife) is a genuinely strong business — 17% adjusted ROE, four straight beats, +26.5% vs SPY over six months — but at 97.14 it has already re-rated, and a defensible 126 target against a defensible 75 bear case is 1.30:1 against a 2.5 floor. Reaching 2.5 needs a $140 target at 13.3x, a multiple MET has not held, which is the reverse-engineering strategy.md forbids. EQT was rejected because the evidence points the wrong way: six insider sales totalling $6.4M against zero buys, a Q2 miss breaking a run of three double-digit beats, and -31% vs SPY over six months. No intraday idea exists because every index feed failed (below). SEVEN OF THE ELEVEN ARE POSITION MANAGEMENT RATHER THAN NEW RISK — GLD, LULU, NKE, BCC and LCII are exits; SPY, DVN, CCJ and SVRA are holds or amendments. Only TLT (a new short) and XLE (an unchanged, still-unfilled level first published 2026-08-15) add exposure. That is deliberate. Twelve positions were open, SIX WITH NO STOP AT ALL, into a week containing a hiking FOMC, and three of them were correlated rate-sensitive consumer/housing longs taken before the regime flipped. Cutting that correlation is the most valuable thing in today's report; it is not a thin day dressed up.

WHY THE NEW-IDEA COUNT IS TWO. Six sector shorts with correct mechanisms were rejected for the same reason — the reward-to-risk only cleared by targeting fresh multi-month lows, i.e. by paying for the part that already happened. Homebuilders (ITB/LEN, group -16 to -19% off highs), airlines (JETS/DAL/UAL/LUV, -17 to -26%), defense (LMT/NOC/LHX/ITA, -11 to -46%), the AI complex (four of six names -22 to -42%), APOG, and gold as a short rather than the exit it became. NVDA at -7.7% was the only AI name with room left and was still not published: its ratio lands on exactly 2.00 and no further, there is no NVDA-specific catalyst (the news is about SoftBank's stake and OpenAI's IPO timing), and it would have been a third equity-beta short alongside SPY and TLT.

RATIO CLUSTERING — FLAGGING IT ON MYSELF. Four of the six ideas carrying a ratio land in a narrow band just above the 2.0 swing floor: TLT 2.14, DVN 2.19, SPY 2.19, XLE 2.33. That band is the known signature of targets fitted to clear the bar, so it is disclosed rather than left for the reader to notice. Two facts cut against the suspicion. First, five of those six sets of levels were published on earlier dates and are carried forward UNCHANGED today — SPY from 2026-08-31, DVN from 2026-09-11, XLE from 2026-08-15, SVRA from 2026-08-23 — so they were not tuned against this morning's prices; only TLT's levels were set today. Second, the research phase re-derived every stop in ATRs FROM THE FILLED ENTRY rather than from the last price and caught itself getting one wrong: CCJ's 88.50 stop was 2.17 ATR measured from 96.68 but only 1.46 ATR from the 94.00 entry, below the 2.0 floor. It was widened to 86.00 (2.13 ATR), which LOWERED the ratio from 4.36 to 3.00 — the correction went against the ratio, which is the direction that matters. The old 135 CCJ target was withdrawn to 118 for the same reason. Every ratio above has been recomputed here from the final entry, target and stop; all six clear their floors, all six stops clear their ATR floors (SPY at 1.88 and XLE at 1.99 against a 1.8 ETF floor are the two thin ones, disclosed rather than tightened, because tightening a stop is the free way to flatter a ratio), and every win_probability beats its 1/(1+R:R) baseline without claiming more than 19 points of edge.

CORRELATION CAP. Read on new and held risk, not on exits: rates/Fed carries TLT and SPY (two), the oil supply shock carries DVN and XLE with CCJ adjacent on energy security (three), and SVRA is the one genuinely uncorrelated holding. The five exits all REDUCE correlated exposure, so counting them against the cap would forbid de-risking — which is the opposite of what the cap is for. IYR SELL_SHORT @ 103.60 was deliberately not re-pitched despite being more right at a 5% 10-year than when it was published, precisely because TLT and SPY already fill the rates lane.

RANKING NOTE. Ranked by conviction, then reward-to-risk. The five exits carry no ratio by construction (there is no target — the instruction is to close), so within their conviction tier they sit below the ideas that do carry one, ordered by catalyst proximity. LULU at rank 7 is arguably the single most urgent action in the book — the worst holding at -13.9%, no stop, and a 5.87% daily ATR going into retail sales and an FOMC on the same morning — but conviction ranks first and its evidence supports a 3, so it is not promoted.

SOURCES THAT FAILED, AND WHAT EACH COST. (1) NO INDEX DATA AT ALL, the whole run: yahoo returned HTTP 429 on ^GSPC, ^NDX, ^DJI, ^RUT and ^VIX, finnhub refuses index CFDs as a subscription product, and stooq 404s them. There is no fetched SPX, VIX, DXY, WTI or 10-year quote in this report. Rates come from FRED at a 2026-09-10/11 vintage and index and commodity levels come from sourced news recaps — every such level in `market_context.levels` is labelled with its provenance, and none is presented as a live fetch. This is the direct reason NO /MES OR /MNQ IDEA WAS PUBLISHED even though the Nasdaq-vs-S&P split overnight (NQ -1.2/-1.7% against ES -0.5/-0.7%) was the most interesting thing on the screen and universe.md prefers futures for exactly that view: setting an entry, stop and target off a remembered index level would be fabricating three numbers on a leveraged instrument. (2) NO EVENT CONTRACTS. `market_data.py events` returned count=0 for FEDDECISION, FOMC, "Fed hike", KXFED, "Fed funds", "interest rate", CPI, recession, rate, oil, Brent and gas, and returned unrelated sports markets for "Fed". The three open KXFEDDECISION positions therefore COULD NOT BE MARKED OR RE-PRICED today, and no event idea is published in a week where a Fed contract would have been the cleanest expression available. (3) yahoo options API returned HTTP 401, so there is NO OPTIONS-IMPLIED MOVE behind any idea here. (4) nasdaq's short-interest endpoint timed out, so NO IDEA IN THIS REPORT CITES A SHORT-INTEREST OR DAYS-TO-COVER READ — that gap is why MU was passed over rather than shorted. (5) `history` failed for CTRA and SWN, truncating the natural-gas screen. Sources that did work: FRED, finnhub (equity/ETF quotes, insider transactions, analyst trends, earnings calendar), nasdaq historical (every level and ATR14 in this report), coingecko, federalreserve.gov, BLS and Census.

PRICES. Synthesis ran pre-market on a Monday with US equities closed, so every `last_price` is the 2026-09-11 close, re-fetched from finnhub at synthesis and confirmed unchanged against the research phase's read. That is a closed market, not stale data. Gold and crude moved materially overnight and the GLD idea says so in its thesis rather than pretending 398.77 is this morning's price.

VERIFIED AND UNRESOLVED. The 81-90% hike odds that four ideas rest on came in second-hand and were checked directly: CME FedWatch 85.6% for 2026-09-16, up from 48.4% on 2026-08-11, with the FOMC date and its SEP status confirmed at the Fed's own calendar. The range holds. Two things did not resolve and are flagged rather than hidden. On August CPI, two sources disagree on whether core +0.3% m/m was an upside surprise or in line; the LEVELS agree (3.4% y/y headline, +0.3% m/m core) and NO RECOMMENDATION HERE CLAIMS A CPI SURPRISE — the rate move is attributed to the oil shock plus hike repricing. On the war, Al Jazeera reported no ceasefire on 2026-09-12 while a barchart headline referenced a US-Iran ceasefire announcement just before the strike; the two could not be reconciled, so the war state is treated as unknown. The Saudi repair timeline is undisclosed, and the only precedent available — an April 2026 pumping-station strike fixed in three days — argues this oil spike could reverse violently and fast. That risk is written into the DVN and XLE key_risk fields rather than left in a footnote. Two dates carried by ideas are explicitly unconfirmed and say so on the idea itself: NKE's next earnings date is not on the fetched 12-day calendar, and SVRA has no verified dated catalyst on any calendar fetched. BCC's Thursday catalyst is listed on the weekly calendar only as "housing data" — the Census starts-and-permits release is the expected content but was not confirmed, and the idea's wording was amended in synthesis to say so. RED TEAM (phase 2c), 11 ideas in, 10 out. Prices, ATRs, SMAs and 120-day extremes were re-pulled for every idea and every one of them matched the report exactly; the position P&L arithmetic also checks out on all eleven. Nothing here was fabricated, and the cuts below are about evidence and levels, not about numbers being invented.

CUT CCJ (was rank 5). Its 3.0:1 rests on a 118.00 target that validation flags at 6.38 ATR, beyond the 6.0 swing guide. Bring the target back to a defensible 110 and the ratio is 2.0:1 against a 33% break-even, versus the 30% hit rate the report claims — negative expectancy, which means the idea never cleared the bar and the target was doing the work. Both listed evidence items argue against the position. See the watchlist note: the position is live and unstopped, and cutting the idea does not cut the risk.

DOWNGRADED GLD 4 to 3. The counter_argument rested on "two bullish shocks, two negative responses". GLD closed UP 0.61% on CPI day (398.77 vs 396.36); it faded a 402.53 open, which is a weak session, but the larger fall came the session BEFORE the print. One data point — the overnight response to the pipeline strike — not a pattern. The exit still stands on Wednesday's event risk.

DOWNGRADED SPY 4 to 3, on two counts. First, the counter_argument's "second independent shock" was specified as SoftBank -11 to -13% on an OpenAI IPO, with SK Hynix and Samsung figures. The cited source carries none of those numbers and names a different driver — a unified call from a group of AI CEOs to slow development. The direction holds (Nasdaq futures -1.7% against S&P -0.7%, Tokyo and Seoul -1% to -3%, all in the source) so the unsourced specifics were removed rather than the argument. Second, and more useful to a reader: the remaining reward-to-risk is 0.74:1, not 2.19:1. The 2.19 is measured from the 773.00 fill; from 764.29 there are 14.29 points to target against 19.21 to the stop. The trim moves forward to the 50-day at 758.62. The stop is NOT moved — manufacturing the ratio back by walking the stop in is the exact failure this phase exists to catch.

CORRECTED SVRA win_probability 0.30 to 0.25. Nothing in the thesis justifies a 66% move inside the horizon and no dated catalyst was verified; expectancy against the 22% break-even is +0.13R and that is the honest figure. Held at conviction 2 and 1%.

TWO VALIDATION FAILURES ARE ARTIFACTS, CHECKED AND CLEARED. LCII's catalyst-date failure compares against LCII's own 2026-10-28 earnings; the catalyst is THO's print, confirmed on the fetched calendar for 2026-09-22 before the open. CCJ's earnings warning is the same shape — the catalyst was UEC, confirmed 2026-09-25 after the close. Separately, BCC's 25.18% and SVRA's 22.96% spread failures are pre-market quote artifacts on a closed market; BCC turns $23.1m a day. And the source 404 that failed all eleven ideas was transient rate-limiting: api.nasdaq.com returned 200 for every one of those URLs on re-test. Those citations have been repointed at the equivalent www.nasdaq.com historical pages, all re-tested at 200, because a bare API path is not something a reader can open. That is why validation_summary reads 0 passed / 11 failed — one shared citation fetch, not eleven broken ideas.

CONFIRMED AT SOURCE. The load-bearing macro claim — a 25bp HIKE at 81% on Kalshi and ~90% on CME FedWatch — is on the cited Kalshi page and is accurate as published. The Saudi East-West pipeline shutdown, the Hormuz closure it was routing around, and "will not retaliate for now" at Baghdad's request are all confirmed on the cited Al Jazeera report, which is DVN's and XLE's whole catalyst. Brent 107.18 up 2.5% and almost 9% on the week is confirmed.

CORRELATION, SAID RATHER THAN CUT. This book is two bets. DVN and XLE are one oil-supply position at 5% combined. SPY short and TLT short are one Fed-hike position at 5% combined, and GLD, LULU, NKE, BCC and LCII are the same view expressed as exits. No cut was made for this, deliberately: five of the ten are closures of unstopped longs, and closing correlated exposure is the correct response to a concentrated book, not a duplicate of it. But size DVN+XLE as one idea and SPY+TLT as one idea, not as four. If Wednesday's statement is a hike-and-done, the whole right-hand side of this report is wrong at once.

NOT CUT, AND DELIBERATELY SO. TLT is the best-constructed idea in the book and keeps conviction 4: the entry does not exist unless 80.665 breaks, so a wrong thesis costs nothing, and its 2.65 ATR stop is the only one clear of the band where this report's stop-outs cluster. DVN keeps conviction 4 on a verified catalyst and honest levels. The five exits stand as written — LULU in particular, an unstopped 13.9% loser with a 5.87% daily ATR going into FOMC and retail sales in the same week, is the most useful instruction in the report.
